clue.text: A contrivance set on foot in the squeeze

definitions.text: A contrivance set on foot in the squeeze

parts.words: A contrivance set on foot in the squeeze
parts.note: a gadget placed at the heel to help ease a foot into a tight-fitting shoe

explanation.surface: Some scheme is launched amid a financial squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set on foot' sounds like 'launched' and 'squeeze' like a credit squeeze; literally it is a tool used at the foot when the shoe is tight.
explanation.definitionFit: The tool is a curved scoop that slides a heel into a snug shoe.

clue.text: Skinhead after a drink in the bushes

indicators.note: after places the skin's head letter behind the drink

parts.note: shrub is an old cordial of fruit juice and spirits
the head of the word skin is S

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed youth hiding in the shrubbery after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: SHRUB is an old drink of fruit and rum; 'Skinhead' gives the head of 'skin', S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrubs are woody plants smaller than trees, i.e. bushes.

clue.text: Decorated or not, are odd-looking

indicators.note: odd-looking suggests the words not and are appear strangely jumbled

explanation.surface: Whether adorned or not, they look strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link; 'odd-looking' rearranges NOT and ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornate is elaborately decorated.

clue.text: Legal term for a man and woman

definitions.meaning: one of the sittings of the English courts, beginning in January
a first name given to both men and women

explanation.definitionFit: The English legal year has a January sitting of this name, and it is a forename used for either sex.

clue.text: Going back order great changes

indicators.note: changes signals the words order and great are altered into a new form

explanation.surface: Reversing a major order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges ORDER and GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrograde means moving backwards or reverting to a worse state.

clue.text: Writing about the right held by a top player

indicators.note: held by means the following pieces sit inside the player

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis tournament
C is short for circa, about
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on the rights of a leading sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts C and R inside SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long piece of writing, often a tedious one.

clue.text: There's a big fall in optical deterioration

definitions.meaning: a clouding of the lens of the eye

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a great waterfall and a clouding of the eye's lens that impairs sight.

clue.text: No longer quiet and proper and plain

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
p is piano, quiet in music
licit means lawful, proper

explanation.surface: No longer hushed, but decent and simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated plainly and clearly.

clue.text: Get into line-time for beastly training!

parts.note: soldiers dress their ranks, getting into line
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Fall in, it is time for some brutal drilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like 'cruel'; it means 'for beasts', horses.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the training of horses in precise movements, and horses are beasts.

clue.text: Locks obtained in exchange for sterling

indicators.note: in exchange for suggests the word sterling is swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: Locks of hair traded for British money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in exchange for' looks like currency trading; it rearranges STERLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks of hair hanging in curls are known as these.

clue.text: The old should carry some cash-it's essential

indicators.note: should carry means the word for old holds the cash letter inside it

parts.note: stale means old, no longer fresh
P stands for penny, a small amount of cash

explanation.surface: Older people ought to keep a little money on them; it is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should carry' puts P inside STALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic, essential item, as in staple foods.

clue.text: Part of the house which is barely used

definitions.text: Part of the house which is barely used

parts.words: Part of the house which is barely used
parts.note: barely means hardly, but also bare, unclothed: the room where people wash

explanation.surface: A room that hardly gets any use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely used' suggests a neglected room; read it as 'used while bare', naked.
explanation.definitionFit: The room for washing and bathing is where people are naked.

clue.text: Coaches as transport

definitions.meaning: coaches as a verb, instructs or teaches
railway carriages pulled by locomotives, a form of transport

explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to teach, and railway carriages in a line are a means of transport.

clue.text: See regular payment is received by nice Italian

indicators.note: is received by means the see and payment go inside the word for nice

parts.note: fine means nice
lo is an old word meaning see or behold
rent is paid regularly to a landlord

explanation.surface: A regular payment collected in Nice by an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' looks like the French city but is the adjective; 'See' is the old exclamation lo, and 'is received by' wraps the payment pieces in the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Florence is Italian.

clue.text: Disposed for hiding and having fun

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the word for is rearranged

parts.note: a hiding is a beating, as is a licking

explanation.surface: Inclined to a beating, yet enjoying oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed' rearranges FOR into FRO; 'hiding' is a beating, not concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Frolicking means playing about merrily, enjoying oneself.

clue.text: Block outside broadcast, cutting returns in a way

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the way

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: returns means the word for cutting is read backwards

parts.note: curt means brusque or cutting

explanation.surface: A block on outside broadcasting, cutting returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' here means brusque, as in a cutting remark; 'returns' turns that word round and 'in' places it within the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct is to block or hinder.

clue.text: Sent rest off, being most strict

indicators.note: off signals the words sent and rest are put out of order

explanation.surface: Sending someone away to sleep, a severe act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SENT and REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict or severe, so this is the superlative.

clue.text: Claims made over river enjoyment

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the claims above the river

parts.note: pleas are claims or appeals
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Disputes over a river give pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is delight or enjoyment.

clue.text: Clash with the party about a racket

parts.note: a clash is a battle
a do is a party
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A fight at a party causes an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like noise; it is the bat used in the old game of shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the light bat used to hit a shuttlecock in an early form of badminton.

clue.text: Work in Greek the editor searched through

indicators.note: in means the work goes inside the Greek and editor letters

parts.note: ED is short for editor
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A work in Greek that the editor combed through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the work inside the abbreviations; 'Work' is the Latin opus, a convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Groped means felt about blindly, searching by touch.

clue.text: Many a learned man causes hurt

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, many
a mage is a learned man, a magus

explanation.surface: A scholar causes injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives D, Roman 500, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is harm or injury.

clue.text: Wanting to lay about the umpire!

indicators.note: about means the wager goes around the umpire

parts.note: to lay a bet is to wager, so lay means bet
ref is short for referee, an umpire

explanation.surface: Keen to wager with the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like desire; it means lacking. 'about' sets the wager around the umpire.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means deprived or lacking.

clue.text: A warning that includes military force

indicators.note: includes means the word that takes the force inside it

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A warning involving troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts the army engineers inside the word that; 'military force' is the Royal Engineers, a convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace or intimidating statement is a kind of warning.

clue.text: Extension in credit facility provision

parts.note: taken as written
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
providing facility means giving ease

explanation.surface: Extending a bank's credit facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is a growth or enlargement, a rise in size.

clue.text: Advantageous in a house full of children

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words a house full of children

explanation.surface: A busy family home is said to be a boon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning 'house full'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something helpful or of practical benefit is advantageous.

clue.text: Succeed with the underworld set

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for it
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Thriving with a group of gangsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' means follow on and take the place of, not prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to take over their position, supplanting them.

clue.text: Note the queen shows restraint

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written
R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A message saying the monarch shows self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message; it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or chain that ties an animal is a restraint.

clue.text: He's rated possibly forgiving personal support

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of he's rated may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A man judged lenient offers individual backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HESRATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion fixed to a seat to support one's head, as in a car.
